+def split_front_matter(text: str) -> tuple[Optional[str], str]:
+    """
+    Split text into front matter and content separated by '---' delimiters.
+    
+    Args:
+        text: The input text to parse.
+        
+    Returns:
+        A tuple (front_matter, content) where front_matter is the string between
+        the opening and closing '---' delimiters (or None if no front matter),
+        and content is the remaining text after the closing delimiter.
+        
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If an opening '---' delimiter is found but no closing delimiter.
+    """
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    if not lines:
+        return (None, text)
+    
+    # Skip leading empty lines
+    i = 0
+    n = len(lines)
+    while i < n and lines[i].strip() == '':
+        i += 1
+        
+    if i >= n:
+        return (None, text)
+        
+    # Check for opening delimiter
+    if lines[i].strip() != '---':
+        return (None, text)
+        
+    # Search for closing delimiter
+    j = i + 1
+    while j < n:
+        if lines[j].strip() == '---':
+            # Found closing delimiter
+            front_matter_lines = lines[i+1:j]
+            content_lines = lines[j+1:]
+            front_matter = ''.join(front_matter_lines)
+            content = ''.join(content_lines)
+            return (front_matter, content)
+        j += 1
+        
+    # If we get here, opening delimiter was found but not closed
+    raise ValueError("Unclosed front matter")
+
+
+def parse_front_matter(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """
+    Parse front matter text into a dictionary of key-value pairs.
+    
+    Args:
+        text: The front matter text (without the delimiters).
+        
+    Returns:
+        A dictionary mapping keys to values. Comment lines (starting with '#')
+        and empty lines are ignored.
+    """
+    result = {}
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
+            continue
+        if ':' not in stripped:
+            continue
+        key, value = stripped.split(':', 1)
+        result[key.strip()] = value.strip()
+    return result
+
